pr_title: Allow disruptive conformance tests and tag 2 as such
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
- Adjusts tooling to allow disrutpive tests to be marked conformance
 - Adds the disruptive tag to both tests (disruptive due to tainting
nodes and evicting other workloads)

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #82663
Fixes #82787

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
Conformance tests may now include disruptive tests. If you are running tests against a live cluster, consider skipping those tests tagged as `Disruptive` to avoid non-test workloads being impacted. Be aware, skipping any conformance tests (even disruptive ones) will make the results ineligible for consideration for the CNCF Certified Kubernetes program.
```
pr_comments:
@neolit123 @Huang-Wei @spiffxp 

Seems to be confusion about if/why this would be evicting non-test related workloads. I've been told if it removes the taint in <300s then it shouldn't evict anything. However, a Sonobuoy user reported exactly that (they could see that the NoExecute manager evicted sonobuoy itself, killing their run).

Some of the tests seem (to my naive eye) to be removing the taint in ~75s but at the same time seem to be expecting actual evictions, so I dont know how that plays with the idea that 300s is a threshold we can count on.

So open questions:
 - are both of these tests actually disruptive due to the taints/evictions (unclear)
 - If they are disruptive they can't be conformance (I think everyone agrees on this one)

/hold

> If they are disruptive they can't be conformance (I think everyone agrees on this one)

+1

> are both of these tests actually disruptive due to the taints/evictions (unclear)

we should get feedback from sig-scheduling on this.
according to the sonobuoy reports you gave they are, i guess.
I disagree
/assign @Huang-Wei

Conformance tests test providers, not arbitrary user clusters.

Conformance demonstrates that providers are able to provide clusters configured in such a way that they provide standard behavior.

There are all kinds of ways that arbitrary clusters could be configured such that they wouldn't pass.

@bgrant0607 
> Conformance tests test providers, not arbitrary user clusters.

i guess this requires a much larger discussion

/assign @timothysc @spiffxp @johnbelamaric

> There are all kinds of ways that arbitrary clusters could be configured such that they wouldn't pass.

That's true, but I'm not certain what you mean by it. It seems like you're implying that just because some configurations wouldn't pass conformance, that the k8s-provided test suite need-not be runnable by a users clusters? 

IMO a user should be able to run the tests to _see_ if their cluster is in a good state or not. It should be runnable with minimal side-effects and minimal requirements. It is fine with me if we want to _fail_ lots of configurations, but the users should be able to run the tests against their own cluster without their own workloads being greatly impacted.

@johnSchnake Running the suite against user clusters is a change of intent of the test suite.

The conformance and certification program is set up to vet cluster management tools, distributions, and services.
The intent is documented here: https://www.cncf.io/certification/software-conformance/

We have made efforts to be minimally disruptive with conformance tests. For example the newly added webhook tests limit their operations to a specific namespace, and the nodeport tests intentionally limit the number of nodeports checked on the data plane to just a couple nodes.

As mentioned in Slack, there is no explicit rule against conformance tests being disruptive. Personally I have always thought of them as needing to be able to be run in an arbitrary cluster; I think I inferred this from the "no special privileges" rule. I think our jobs in creating the conformance suite becomes a lot easier if we can relax the idea that they can run in an arbitrary cluster.

In fact we need to be able to test disruptive behaviors. This gets back to being able to categorize the tests ("profiles") better.

Given the lack of rule - perhaps the solution in this case is not to demote the tests, but rather to additionally mark them as `Disruptive`?

There was an attempt to distinguish between different types of test suites here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/3361/files

It should be tag'd as [Disruptive] IMO, and I think it would be fine to leave in conformance.

Folks wanting to validate their provider will have to accept this as a criteria, and those wanting to run the suite on their cluster in the wild can default to excluding.
I agree with @timothysc: let's create a new tag. In general, we need to add a lot more tags.

Based on the apparent agreement of feedback; I've just updated this to add the disruptive tag.

I want to note that this does have implications for users in a way since the CNCF instructions specify to run `sonobuoy run` to run the appropriate conformance tests (since historically that excluded things like disruptive/flaky/alpha tests). If we want to have overlap there we may have to revisit those instructions (and some Sonobuoy options/messaging) to the user to ensure users know when/why they may have disruptive tests being run on their cluster.
Updated the PR message and commit message as well.

i think there was an effort recently to remove some tests from conformance that were alpha, disruptive and flaky.

@BenTheElder do you know the details on that?
@johnSchnake - we should update the instructions for running for CNCF certification vs. running in the wild.

@timothysc I've made https://github.com/heptio/sonobuoy/issues/877 and we need to decide naming/defaults.  I'm leaning towards having the non-destructive route be the default, but that wouldn't be valid for certification which may lead to some frustration.

Likewise, if we make the default _all_ the conformance tests, someone running these in the wild will be (maybe more) frustrated that some destructive tests were run by default.
/retest

@neolit123 @timothysc @johnbelamaric So the `walk_test.go` file actually automated the fact that `[Disruptive]` tests cant be conformance and so the automated script to generate the conformance list won't recognize these tests.

Should I, in this PR, also be making disruptive tests allowed via that code?

It just seems like we are very close to the v1.16 release and we don't have clear agreement about whether or not this test should be disruptive, why it is disruptive, or if disruptive tests should be conformance tests.

Unsure how to proceed.

> So the walk_test.go file actually automated the fact that [Disruptive] tests cant be conformance and so the automated script to generate the conformance list won't recognize these tests.

no, that was the whole point to allow the limitation (i.e. not allow disruptive tests to be recognized). @spiffxp has more context. if a test is disruptive it's not conformance and your observation proves that.

> It just seems like we are very close to the v1.16 release and we don't have clear agreement about whether or not this test should be disruptive, why it is disruptive, or if disruptive tests should be conformance tests.

i'm bringing this to #sig-release.

@johnSchnake @neolit123 is there a change we can make to the test for it to avoid the scenario where the pod that is running the e2e conformance tests do not get nuked? (like look up the "current" node using downard api and avoid scheduling the test pod in the current node?)

>  is there a change we can make to the test for it to avoid the scenario where the pod that is running the e2e conformance tests do not get nuked? 

I don't think that approach is terribly useful; it avoids one issue in some situations:
 - What if it is a 2 node cluster (1 master 1 worker); are those no longer capable of conformance? Or they'll still just hit this issue anyways? Do we fail since we can't avoid restarting the e2e pod? Do we warn and do it anyways?
 - 1 node clusters couldn't pass conformance anyways, but it would still cause the e2e pod to get evicted anyways (or fail/warn like above)
 - What about other workloads besides the e2e pod? (prod workloads, sonobuoy workload, etc).

I've already committed a PR to Sonobuoy so that we tolerate this taint and launch the e2e plugin to tolerate this taint. It is a bit of a stopgap but I feel like if we are going to allow 'destructive' tests then it makes sense to at least clearly document/limit the ways in which they intend to be destructive so that users can mitigate any risks.

@johnSchnake i guess then decision is made already based on @bgrant0607 and @johnbelamaric 's notes above. Also the existing rule we have that we should *not* have any tags for conformance tests. Only thing left now is to document what was said earlier.

(at least for 1.16)

Also, on the topic of what conformance is for, @bgrant0607 gave a link to https://www.cncf.io/certification/software-conformance/ but despite describing all the benefits for being run for providers etc etc it also says:

> Confirmability: any end user can confirm that their distribution or platform remains conformant by running the identical open source conformance application (Sonobuoy) that was used to certify.

Which seems to indicate an intent/capability to run them on a prod cluster.
@johnSchnake let's fix that doc to reflect the current discussion.

We have 2 days before the release and currently, by default, run secretly disruptive tests in a conformance run.

IMO that is the worst possible case; the alternatives:
1. demote the 2 tests (temporarily maybe) and resolve this after v1.16
2.  allow destructive+conformance tests
    - update the scripts that generate the conformance list to allow this _NEW_ behavior
    - update the cncf documentation about how to get certification
    - update Sonobuoy to support this appropriately/safely
    - add the tags to the test

Due to the larger scope of (2) and the short time horizon, I advocate for (1). Even if that means we pursue (2) right after the release, it seems too rushed a decision to make on the deadline we have.

Thoughts?

See updated ticket with information about resolution. TL;DR; we are leaving tests as-is (mis-tagged) for v1.16 and dealing with it.

This PR is now targeted for v1.17 and includes the changes to support disruptive conformance tests based on the conversations I've had about the issue.

/hold

Waiting for confirmation during a conformance-wg meeting that this is 100% the direction to go. Seems like we have a fair amount of consensus on slack though.

FYI it would be the conformance subproject of SIG-arch that decides, not the CNCF conformance-wg.

I think that's what you meant anyway, but want to make it clear. I see you already added it to the [agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W31nXh9RYAb_VaYkwuPLd1hFxuRX3iU0DmaQ4lkCsX8/edit#heading=h.l87lu17xm9bh). Thanks!
/priority important-soon

This was discussed in the conformance-wg meeting; there was agreement that this is appropriate (to have disruptive conformance tests) so I'm removing the hold.

/hold cancel
/retest
/assign

/lgtm

(re-applying after rebase)

issue_context.title: Allow conformance tests to be marked as Disruptive
issue_context.body:
**What would you like to be added**:
Our tooling that makes the list of conformance tests needs to allow conformance tests to be marked as disruptive.

**Why is this needed**:
To test default, conformance behavior which may be disruptive (e.g. taint eviction)

ref #82663

/sig testing
/area conformance

review_comments:
Per our talk on [Slack](https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C09TP78DV/p1568310289067700), these 2 conformance tests are relatively "non-disruptive" (comparing to other taint tests in this file) as they internally cancel the taint within default toleraionSeconds (300 secs), which means:

1. when the taint is applied, under the hood the e2e irrelative pods will be put into an eviction queue holding them up for 300 seconds.
2. the e2e taint gets canceled, then the pods in the eviction queue will be released - i.e. they will be exactly the same as before.

So my impression is that some cases in this file are more qualified to be applied as "[Disruptive]" label.

I am definitely not versed in how the scheduling/eviction works, but I'm just confused because your description doesn't seem to square with what is happening.

I didn't trust my understanding so I wanted to repro it myself. I built the kind images for the v1.16.0-rc.2 tag and ran just the `removing taint cancels eviction` test and reprod that the sonobuoy pod (a workload outside the test framework) gets evicted.

Here are some of the logs from the controller:
```
0913 18:54:07.405937       1 taint_manager.go:105] NoExecuteTaintManager is deleting Pod: heptio-sonobuoy/sonobuoy-e2e-job-3223075635be415d
I0913 18:54:07.406113       1 taint_manager.go:105] NoExecuteTaintManager is deleting Pod: heptio-sonobuoy/sonobuoy
I0913 18:54:07.406147       1 taint_manager.go:105] NoExecuteTaintManager is deleting Pod: kube-system/kindnet-lpx4w
I0913 18:54:07.406675       1 event.go:255] Event(v1.ObjectReference{Kind:"Pod", Namespace:"heptio-sonobuoy", Name:"sonobuoy", UID:"", APIVersion:"", ResourceVersion:"", FieldPath:""}): type: 'Normal' reason: 'TaintManagerEviction' Marking for deletion Pod heptio-sonobuoy/sonobuoy
I0913 18:54:07.406727       1 event.go:255] Event(v1.ObjectReference{Kind:"Pod", Namespace:"heptio-sonobuoy", Name:"sonobuoy-e2e-job-3223075635be415d", UID:"", APIVersion:"", ResourceVersion:"", FieldPath:""}): type: 'Normal' reason: 'TaintManagerEviction' Marking for deletion Pod heptio-sonobuoy/sonobuoy-e2e-job-3223075635be415d
```

Is this a bug? I see the eviction/deletion of the pod happen even before it logs that it is marking it for eviction.

I think everyone here would welcome a PR if it made the tags more appropriate on the rest of the tests.  These two, being conformance related, have just a higher priority so I want to be sure to handle them for the release.
Please split changes to this file into a separate PR.
I kind of think this is fine right now and shouldn't affect the suite.
OK, I rebased onto master. Left this in the PR for now unless the request is reinforced.
